headline: Sensex and Nifty crash as US bond yields hit 24-year high and FIIs sell off Indian stocks

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: US 10-year bond yields hitting a 24-year high rattling domestic markets
En-masse selling of Indian stocks by foreign institutional investors
Global rate hike bets fueled by energy shocks and eurozone bond pressure
Concerns over oil prices and global rate hikes sparking capital outflows
whatHappening: Sensex crashed 1,000 points, wiping out approximately Rs 9 lakh crore in investor wealth
Indian share benchmarks are on track for their longest weekly losing run in 25 years
The Nifty Auto index dropped over 4% as major auto stocks faced selling pressure
Inox Air Products and Anarock Property Consultants filed IPO papers with Sebi
summary: The Indian stock market faced a severe downturn with the Sensex plunging 1,000 points due to surging US bond yields and heavy FII selling. While Tata Motors fell over 3% despite strong sales growth, Adani Green Energy expanded its battery storage capacity. The market is currently witnessing its worst losing streak in decades amid global economic uncertainty.
